title: Cleaning audit: inspecting, recording and signing off a clean
moduleTitle: Group (Cleaning & Hygiene): Quality, evidence and handover
audience: Supervisors and cleaners who inspect finished work in any cleaning-group business, including anyone who signs off a clean before handover to a customer.
learningOutcomes: Describe the order of an audit, from reading the standard to signing off the area.
Check a cleaned area against the quality standard in the relevant SOP and the agreed job brief for that customer.
Record each defect with its location, its type and the action it needs, and take photographs where the business requires them.
Decide whether a defect needs a re-clean, a follow-up or an escalation, and record the outcome.

instruction.heading: Status of this lesson
instruction.body: The uploaded source gives the title of a cleaning audit annex but not its text. This lesson is a general outline written by the team. A completed audit is not a licence, a certificate or an authority for any regulated work.

instruction.heading: What an audit is for
instruction.body: An audit checks finished work against a standard before it is handed over. It catches defects while the cleaner who did the work can still correct them, and it gives the business evidence that the work met the scope. An audit looks at the area against the same standard each time. It is not a personal judgement of the cleaner who did the work.

instruction.heading: The standard you audit against
instruction.body: Each area is audited against three things: the quality standard in the relevant SOP, the agreed job brief for that customer, and any requirement that applies to that particular site. Read all three before you start. If the standard is unclear for an area, stop and ask your supervisor rather than inventing a standard of your own.

instruction.heading: Walking the audit
instruction.body: Start at the entrance or another fixed point and move in one direction, so that nothing is missed. Check surfaces at the height people use them and in the light they use them. Check the detail as well as the main floor or surface: edges, skirting boards, corners, fixtures, the back of doors and the washroom fittings. Check the equipment and the storage area used for the job, as well as the work area itself.

instruction.heading: Recording defects and scores
instruction.body: Record each defect separately, with its location, its type and a short description. Typical types include a smear, a missed area, a residue, damage, a safety issue and an equipment fault. Where the business uses a score, apply it the same way to every area. A safety issue is never offset by a good score elsewhere. It is stopped and reported before anything else happens.

instruction.heading: Photographs
instruction.body: Photograph a defect where the business's evidence rules require it, for example before and after a re-clean, or to record damage. Take each photograph from the same position every time, and include a clear reference such as the room name or the fixture. Do not photograph people, or customer property beyond what the record needs.

instruction.heading: Acting on what the audit finds
instruction.body: Decide the action for each defect: re-clean it now, schedule a follow-up, change the method or the equipment, or escalate it to the supervisor. Record the action and the person who will take it. Do not sign an area off while it has an open safety issue or an open re-clean.

instruction.heading: Sign-off and handover
instruction.body: Sign an area off only when every defect has been resolved, or has been recorded with an agreed follow-up. The sign-off record names the area, the date, the auditor, the standard that was used, any open items and, where it applies, the customer representative.

instruction.heading: Legal position
instruction.body: This lesson does not set any statutory basis for an audit. Where an audit is used to show that a legal duty has been met, or where a customer contract requires it, the rules that apply in each state and territory have not yet been confirmed here, so check with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.

procedure: Read the quality standard, the agreed job brief and any site requirement for the area before you start.
Check that the audit form, the light and the photography device the business uses are ready, and that your own equipment is clean.
Confirm that any open safety issue from the last visit has been resolved before you start.
Walk the area in one direction from a fixed start point.
Check each surface and fixture against the standard, including the edges, corners and detail points.
Check the equipment and the storage area used for the job.
Record each defect with its location, its type and a short description.
For any safety issue, stop the audit of that area and report it before you record anything else for that area.
Photograph defects where the evidence rules require it, from the same position each time.
Decide the action for each defect, and record who will take it.
Sign off only when every open item is resolved or has an agreed follow-up.
File the audit record with the job record.

workedExamples.situation: On a final audit of an office floor you find a streak across the carpet tiles and a patch of residue near a door.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which defects do you record, and what action does each need?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record each defect on its own line with its location and type. The streak is a re-clean if the standard calls for a smear-free finish. The residue is also a re-clean, and you check that the product used suits the surface. Do not sign the area off until both are resolved or an agreed follow-up is recorded.

workedExamples.situation: During the audit you notice a damaged socket cover beside a washroom sink.
workedExamples.reasoning: A damaged electrical fitting is a safety issue. Stop the audit of that area, keep people away from the socket, and report it to your supervisor before you continue. Do not clean around the fitting, and do not sign the washroom off while the issue is open.

workedExamples.situation: You audit a lift interior and find a smear on the panel that you cleaned yourself an hour ago.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Record the defect, re-clean it using the method in the relevant SOP, and check it again. Checking your own work is useful, but where the business's process requires a second person to sign off, the sign-off waits for that person.

equipmentAndPpe: The audit form or checklist that the business uses.
The quality standard and the agreed job brief for the area.
A torch or task light for checking surfaces and corners.
A camera or device for photographs, where the business requires them.
Gloves and any other protective equipment the area requires.

commonErrors.error: Auditing from memory rather than from the standard.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the standard and the scope before you start, every time.

commonErrors.error: Recording one overall pass or fail with no list of defects.
commonErrors.prevention: Record each defect with its location and type, even when the score is high.

commonErrors.error: Signing off an area that still has an open safety issue.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, report, and hold the sign-off until the issue is closed.

commonErrors.error: Checking only the main floor and missing the edges and fixtures.
commonErrors.prevention: Walk the area in one direction and check each detail point the standard lists.

commonErrors.error: Taking a photograph that does not show which room or fixture it is.
commonErrors.prevention: Name the room or fixture in the record, and take each photograph from the same position.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Any safety issue found during an audit is stopped and reported before the audit of that area continues. A good score does not outweigh a safety issue.
Do not carry out electrical, height or other regulated work to correct a defect found in an audit. Report it instead.
Check the period for which audit records are kept, and any evidence rule that applies to audits, with the relevant regulator before relying on this point.
Photographs of premises must not capture people or customer property beyond what the record needs.

qualityStandard: The standard and the agreed job brief are read and applied before the audit starts.
Every defect is recorded on its own, with its location, its type and its action.
No area is signed off while it has an open safety issue or an open re-clean.
Photographs follow the business's evidence rule and include a clear reference to the area.
documentationEvidence: Completed audit form for each area, showing the standard that was used.
Defect list with the location, type, action and the person responsible for each defect.
Photographs with a room or fixture reference, where the business requires them.
Sign-off record showing the date, the auditor and any open items.
summary: Read the standard, the scope and any site requirement before you audit.
Record each defect on its own, with its location, its type and its action.
Stop and report any safety issue before you record anything else for that area.
Sign an area off only when every open item is resolved or has an agreed follow-up.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the first step before you start an audit of a cleaned area?
options: Read the quality standard, the agreed job brief and any site requirement for the area
Sign the sheet so the audit is recorded as started and the date and time are noted
Walk to the far end of the area so you finish there first and check the sinks and taps first

knowledgeChecks.question: During an audit you find a damaged electrical fitting near a washroom sink. What do you do?
options: Clean around the fitting and note it on the form at the end and move on to the next room
Sign off the washroom now and report the fitting later once the area is clean
Stop, keep people away from it, and report it to your supervisor before you continue

knowledgeChecks.question: A defect is found in a room you cleaned yourself an hour ago. What is the correct action?
options: Leave it, because the room was cleaned recently and is probably fine for guests
Record the defect, re-clean it using the relevant SOP, and check again before any sign-off
Remove the entry from the form so the record looks clean before the form is filed away
Ask the customer to accept the room as it is and sign the form for the client
